records.vts_name: Fundy Traffic (Bay of Fundy VTS Zone)
records.vts_authority: Canadian Coast Guard (MCTS); zone established by Transport Canada regulation SOR/2025-275
records.vts_sector: Sectors 1 and 2 (Ch 14 and Ch 12); TSS entrance/exit calling-in points 1A/1B (sector 1), 4E, 5A/5B (sector 2)
records.vts_boundary_basis: SOR/2025-275 Sch. 3 item 7 and RAMN 2026 Part 3 s.3.7.3.7 define the Bay of Fundy VTS Zone. RAMN Table 3-30 calling-in points 1A 'Southwest entrance to traffic separation scheme' (44°10'40.3"N 066°48'16"W) and 1B 'Southwest exit' (44°16'09.3"N 066°53'54"W) lie on the zone's outer boundary segments (own check: each is the midpoint of the boundary segment between the listed turning points), and 4E and 5A/5B mark the TSS entrance/exit and north exit/entrance inside sectors 2. The TSS therefore lies wholly within the zone, starting at its outer limit. Fundy Traffic monitors by radar and AIS.
records.reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system in this region (project Part I list: none for Canada). Sailing plans and position reports under SOR/2025-275 Part 4 are the reporting duties of the VTS zone itself, so they are recorded under the VTS, not as a separate MRS.
records.tss_name: In the Bay of Fundy and approaches
records.evidence_summary: Statutory VTS zone (SOR/2025-275) and CCG RAMN 2026 calling-in points expressly name the TSS southwest entrance/exit and north entrance/exit; Fundy Traffic, operated from Halifax MCTS, monitors the zone by radar and AIS. No Part I reporting system applies.
records.source_date: SOR/2025-275 current to 2026-09-21; RAMN 2026 page modified 2026-09-25
records.prior_lead_outcome: corrected: VTS only confirmed, but the zone reporting is recorded as part of the VTS (not national MRS) and the centre is Halifax MCTS (Canso Traffic is a different zone); no part of the TSS is in US waters (entrance points lie on the Canadian zone boundary).

records.vts_boundary_basis: No USCG VTS or VMRS is established for this area: Table 1 to 33 CFR 161.12(c) lists every VTS and VMRS centre and monitoring area and has none here, and 33 CFR 161.2 defines a VTS as a service implemented by the USCG. NAVCEN's enumerated list of Coast Guard Vessel Traffic Centers and its VTS Locations page also have none. Together these are treated as an official complete list of US VTS that excludes this TSS.
records.reporting_boundary_basis: The TSS lies between about 43°07.8'N and 43°37'N (33 CFR 167.51-53), entirely north of WHALESNORTH, whose northern edge runs from 42°39'N 70°37'W to 42°45'N 70°13'W (33 CFR 169.105). WHALESSOUTH is far to the south. No VMRS applies.
records.unresolved_issue: Classification relies on 33 CFR 161 plus NAVCEN being complete lists of US VTS. Local voluntary arrangements (e.g. pilots, harbour master) not searched.
records.tss_name: In the approaches to Portland, Maine
records.evidence_summary: 33 CFR 161 Table 1 and NAVCEN list no VTS or VMRS at Portland, and 33 CFR 169 coordinates put the TSS outside WHALESNORTH. On these official complete lists, neither association exists.
records.prior_lead_outcome: corrected: prior 'Unresolved' upgraded to 'Neither confirmed' because 33 CFR 161.2 limits VTS to USCG services and 161 Table 1 plus NAVCEN's enumerated VTC list exclude Portland; WHALESNORTH exclusion confirmed.

records.vts_boundary_basis: No USCG VTS or VMRS is established for this area: Table 1 to 33 CFR 161.12(c) lists every VTS and VMRS centre and monitoring area and has none here, and 33 CFR 161.2 defines a VTS as a service implemented by the USCG. records.reporting_scheme_name: Off the north-eastern and south-eastern coasts of the United States: WHALESNORTH (northeastern area)
records.reporting_boundary_basis: Partial. Own geometry check of 33 CFR 167.76-167.77 against 169.105: the separation zone and both lanes stay inside WHALESNORTH from the Boston precautionary area down to the area's southern limit at 41°00'N (crossing at about 069°05'W to 069°11'W), with no crossing of the western or eastern edges. The Boston precautionary area (6.17 NM radius at 42°22.71'N 70°46.97'W) is in Massachusetts Bay inside the area; its innermost harbour edge depends on the undefined 'Massachusetts shoreline' boundary. The lane sections south of 41°00'N and the junction precautionary area (north edge about 40°50.5'N) are outside. Year-round; self-propelled ships of 300 GT or more report once on entry (169.110, 169.125, 169.130).
records.unresolved_issue: Reporting coverage partial: lanes south of 41°00'N and the junction precautionary area shared with Off New York (Nantucket) are outside WHALESNORTH. IMO adopting resolution not cited in 33 CFR 169 (VRS-0021 per project baseline).
records.tss_name: In the approach to Boston, Massachusetts
records.evidence_summary: No USCG VTS at Boston (33 CFR 161 Table 1, NAVCEN). Most of the TSS (all north of 41°00'N) lies within WHALESNORTH, the northeastern area of IMO-adopted VRS-0021, per 33 CFR 169.105 coordinates.
records.prior_lead_outcome: confirmed: MRS only via VRS-0021 WHALESNORTH, partial coverage to 41°00'N re-derived from the CFR coordinates.

records.vts_boundary_basis: No USCG VTS or VMRS is established for this area: Table 1 to 33 CFR 161.12(c) lists every VTS and VMRS centre and monitoring area and has none here, and 33 CFR 161.2 defines a VTS as a service implemented by the USCG. NAVCEN's enumerated list of Coast Guard Vessel Traffic Centers and its VTS Locations page also have none. Together these are treated as an official complete list of US VTS that excludes this TSS. VMRS Buzzards Bay ('Buzzards Bay Control', Ch 11) is a USCG mandatory VMRS, not a VTS. Its area is east and north of the line Sakonnet Point (41°27.20'N 71°11.70'W) to Buzzards Bay Entrance Light (41°23.48'N 71°02.5'W) to Cuttyhunk (41°24.60'N 70°57.00'W). Own calculation: the Buzzards Bay approach separation zone ends at 41°21.80'N 71°07.10'W, about 3.5 NM south of that line, and the lane corners are about 3.3 to 3.8 NM short of it. The Narragansett approach and its precautionary areas (071°23.3'W) are west of Sakonnet Point, so also outside. The VMRS begins beyond the end of the TSS; it adjoins the route but does not cover it.
records.reporting_boundary_basis: VMRS Buzzards Bay does not cover the TSS (see above). WHALESNORTH does not extend west of 69°17'W south of 42°N or south of 41°00'N, so it does not reach this TSS. 33 CFR 165.100 (Northeast District RNA) repeats the VMRS Buzzards Bay rules and does not add a reporting scheme for the TSS.
records.vts_leads: VMRS Buzzards Bay (Buzzards Bay Control) applies only landward of the TSS
records.unresolved_issue: Editorial point for coordinator: VMRS Buzzards Bay adjoins but does not cover the TSS, so it is not linked. Classification relies on 33 CFR 161 plus NAVCEN being complete lists of US VTS.
records.tss_name: In the approaches to Narragansett Bay, Rhode Island, and Buzzards Bay, Massachusetts
records.evidence_summary: No USCG VTS at Narragansett/Buzzards Bay approaches (33 CFR 161 Table 1, NAVCEN). The only nearby mandatory system, VMRS Buzzards Bay, starts about 3.5 NM beyond the northern end of the Buzzards Bay approach. WHALESNORTH does not reach the area.
records.prior_lead_outcome: corrected: prior 'Unresolved' upgraded to 'Neither confirmed'; the VMRS gap (about 3.5 NM beyond the TSS end) re-derived and confirmed.

records.vts_centre: Vessel Traffic Center, Sector New York, Fort Wadsworth, Staten Island
records.vts_sector: New York Traffic, Lower New York Bay monitoring areas (Table 1 to 161.12(c) item 7: Ch 11 sailing plans / Ch 12 anchored; Ch 14 Lower Bay)
records.vts_boundary_basis: Partial. 33 CFR 161.25 bounds VTS New York to the south by a line from Breezy Point through the entrance buoys of Ambrose, Swash and Sandy Hook Channels to Sandy Hook Point. The Table 1 monitoring areas use the same line. Ambrose Channel Lighted Buoy 1 is at 40.46876N 73.87223W (D1 LNM 06/10/2025), about 1.95 NM from the centre of the 7 NM circular precautionary area at 40°27.50'N 73°49.90'W (33 CFR 167.151(a)), so the VTS boundary line runs through the precautionary area. Own approximate estimate: the north-western part of the circle, roughly 8% of its area, lies inside the VTS area. All traffic lanes and separation zones (Eastern, South-eastern and Southern approaches ending at about 40°20'N to 40°28'N, 073°41'W to 073°48'W) and the Nantucket approach and junction area lie outside.
records.reporting_boundary_basis: WHALESNORTH ends at 41°00'N and does not reach the Eastern approach off Nantucket (about 40°22'N to 40°37'N) or the junction precautionary area (north edge about 40°50.5'N). WHALESSOUTH is off Georgia/Florida. VTS New York VMRS reporting is part of the VTS, not a separate MRS.
records.unresolved_issue: Coverage partial (landward sector of the precautionary area only; fraction is own approximation, Swash/Sandy Hook buoy and Breezy/Sandy Hook point positions approximated). Currency: USCG D1 proposed discontinuing Ambrose Channel Buoys 1, 2 and A (comment window to 2026-10-03); if removed, the 161.25 boundary reference needs re-checking.
records.evidence_summary: 33 CFR 161.25 VTS New York area reaches the Ambrose/Swash/Sandy Hook entrance buoys, which lie inside the 7 NM Off New York precautionary area. So VTS New York covers the landward part of that precautionary area only; the lanes are outside. No Part I reporting system applies.
records.source_date: eCFR 2026-09-01; VTS NY User Manual rev. Jan 2023; D1 LNM 2025-06-10 and 2025-09-10
records.prior_lead_outcome: confirmed: VTS only with partial coverage; the open chart question is resolved: Ambrose Channel entrance buoys are about 2 NM inside the 7 NM precautionary area.

records.reporting_boundary_basis: TSS at about 38°27'N to 39°00'N (33 CFR 167.171-174), south of WHALESNORTH (41°00'N) and north of WHALESSOUTH (31°27'N). No VMRS. Maritime Exchange position/ETA reporting is by request (lead only) and not mandatory.

records.unresolved_issue: Maritime Exchange voluntary reporting not verified from an official source. Classification relies on 33 CFR 161 plus NAVCEN being complete lists of US VTS.
records.evidence_summary: No USCG VTS or VMRS at Delaware Bay (33 CFR 161 Table 1, NAVCEN), and the TSS is outside both WHALES areas. The Maritime Exchange's reporting station is a commercial lead, not a VTS or mandatory scheme.

The DW route has only a recommended VHF 16 announcement (167.203(h)).

records.vts_centre: Vessel Traffic Center, Sector Houston-Galveston, southeast Houston
records.vts_sector: Houston Traffic, south of Exxon Dock #1 line (Ch 12; Ch 5A sailing plans)
records.vts_boundary_basis: Partial. The 161.35(a) VTS area includes the Galveston Bay Entrance Channel and Outer Bar Channel. Reporting point 1, Galveston Bay Entrance Channel LB '1C' (29°18.2'N 94°37.6'W), lies inside the TSS inshore precautionary area (own point-in-polygon check against 167.350(a)). The Table 1 monitoring area is the navigable waters north of 29°00'N, west of 94°20'W, south of 29°49'N and east of 95°20'W. Every TSS point lies in that box, but navigable waters end at the 12 NM territorial sea (161.2), and note 4 says watch is not required beyond them. Own approximate calculation from the Galveston entrance jetties: the inshore precautionary area and the landward lane sections (about 4 to 6 NM) are within 12 NM. The seaward lane ends (about 17 NM) and the offshore precautionary area (about 20 NM) are outside. NAVCEN: the area runs 'from the sea buoy'.
records.reporting_boundary_basis: No Part I system in the Gulf of Mexico (VRS-0021 is Atlantic only, 33 CFR 169.105/115). VTS Houston-Galveston VMRS reporting (33 CFR 161 Subpart B) is the VTS's own reporting, not a separate MRS.
records.unresolved_issue: 12 NM limit position computed approximately from jetty/shore positions, not from an official baseline chart; the exact split of the lanes needs a NOAA maritime limits check.
records.tss_name: In the approaches to Galveston Bay
records.evidence_summary: VTS Houston-Galveston's statutory area and reporting point 1 (LB 1C) lie within the TSS inshore precautionary area, and its monitoring area covers the TSS box within US navigable waters. Coverage is partial because the offshore end of the TSS is beyond the 12 NM territorial sea.
records.source_date: eCFR 2026-09-01; VTS HG User Manual rev. March 2025
records.prior_lead_outcome: confirmed: VTS only; refined to partial coverage (offshore precautionary area and seaward lanes beyond navigable waters).

records.vts_name: Centro de Control de Tráfico Marítimo de Veracruz (CCTMVER)
records.vts_authority: Administración del Sistema Portuario Nacional Veracruz (ASIPONA Veracruz), acting as auxiliary to the Capitanía de Puerto de Veracruz
records.vts_centre: CCTM, Av. Marina Mercante No. 210, Veracruz (MMSI 003450310, VHF 10/16)
records.vts_boundary_basis: The ASIPONA 'Área de Influencia' page states that the CCTMVER control area includes the traffic separation zones, lanes and precautionary areas, bounded by 19°15.10'N 096°11.00'W (coast), 19°19.00'N 096°11.00'W, 19°19.00'N 095°46.60'W, 19°02.20'N 095°46.60'W and 19°02.20'N 095°58.10'W (coast). Own check against COLREG.2/Circ.41 (1996): the North Approach (to 19°19.00'N) and the precautionary area are inside. The East Approach lanes run seaward to 095°45.00'W, so on the 1996 coordinates about 1.5 NM of their seaward end lies east of the box limit (095°46.60'W). Recorded as partial despite the page's general statement.
records.reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system for Mexico (project Part I list). No formally named Mexican mandatory ship reporting scheme was found for this area. CCTM services are 'a solicitud' (on request), and the Capitanía de Puerto keeps watch on VHF 12.
records.unresolved_issue: The ASIPONA pages do not use the term VTS and give no legal designation or mandatory participation rule; the service type should be confirmed from SEMAR/Capitanía or ALRS Vol 6. Partial coverage rests on 1996 TSS coordinates, not checked against any amendment in Ships' Routeing 2025. National mandatory reporting search was not exhaustive (SEMAR sources not located).
records.tss_name: In the approaches to the port of Veracruz
records.evidence_summary: ASIPONA Veracruz's official CCTM pages describe a radar (X/S band) and AIS traffic monitoring and navigational assistance centre whose control area expressly includes the TSS zones, lanes and precautionary areas. On the 1996 IMO coordinates, only the seaward tip of the East Approach falls outside its box.
records.prior_lead_outcome: corrected: prior 'Unresolved' with an unnamed radar lead replaced by the ASIPONA Veracruz official CCTM page naming the TSS; classified VTS only (partial), with service designation caveat.

method_notes: US records: eCFR point-in-time XML (2026-09-01) for 33 CFR 161, 165, 167 and 169; own geometry (segment intersection, point-in-polygon, flat-earth distances) on the CFR coordinates. 'Neither confirmed' for five US TSS rests on three things: 33 CFR 161.2 defines a VTS as USCG-implemented; Table 1 to 161.12(c) lists every VTS and VMRS centre; and NAVCEN's overview enumerates the Coast Guard VTCs (its list names 13 places under '12 Vessel Traffic Centers' and omits Lower Mississippi, while the Locations page shows it). The coordinator may prefer 'Unresolved' if that is not accepted as a complete list. Canadian pages via canada.ca failed with curl (HTTP/2 errors) and were fetched with Python urllib. The RAMN 2026 PDF was too large for WebFetch; the HTML Part 3 was used. hacienda.gob.mx failed TLS verification (not bypassed). The Veracruz TSS coordinates are from the 1996 COLREG.2/Circ.41 copy, not the 2025 edition. Notice of Arrival (33 CFR 160 Subpart C) is a port-entry notice, not an area reporting scheme, and is not counted. All accesses 2026-09-29.
